004.en: The ‘Organization and people’ dimension is most concerned with establishing a culture of trust. “Digitally enabled organizations are under pressure to continually improve their performance under changing market conditions. [...]. The challenge for these organizations is to foster an effective set of shared beliefs, perceptions, and values in relation to risks. This, in turn, should create a safety culture, and result in behaviour that is beneficial for all stakeholders, including the members of the organization.” Ref 2.2.1

052.en: How does ITIL collaborate with DevOps practices to support digital product and service management?

053.en: By providing the framework while DevOps supplies practices and techniques

054.en: By replacing DevOps practices with standardized service management processes

055.en: By limiting DevOps usage to software development activities

056.en: By positioning DevOps as a governance framework over ITIL

057.en: “DevOps is a valuable complementary approach which should be used as a source of detailed practical advice enabling such activities of the ITIL Product and Service Lifecycle” explaining that ITIL provides the framework while DevOps supplies practices and techniques. Ref 7.3.1

058.en: Why is project management important within the ITIL framework?

060.en: It replaces product and service management practices

061.en: It supports the implementation and transformation of products and services

062.en: It defines service level targets and metrics

Ref 7.3.2 D. Incorrect. “Service level management” is a distinct ITIL practice, not the purpose of project management. Ref 7.3.2

068.en: ITIL provides service management guidance while PRINCE2 Agile manages project delivery

122.en: Which BEST explains why an organization might choose to utilize external suppliers?

123.en: To obtain capabilities that are difficult to develop internally

124.en: Organizations may utilize external suppliers due to resource scarcity, which includes a lack of needed skills or resources internally. It also allows them to leverage the subject matter expertise and knowledge of the supplier.

125.en: Why is project management important in ITIL?

126.en: To manage routine operational activities and service requests

127.en: To define governance authority across the ITIL Value System

128.en: To deliver time-bound initiatives that introduce new or changed services

129.en: To enable structured delivery of change while services continue to operate

130.en: Project management is essential for delivering change within the ITIL Value System. Effective projects ensure that delivery is structured, controlled, and strategically aligned. PRINCE2 methods specifically support the delivery of changes that implement or modify products and services.

131.en: A telecom provider designs an enterprise package that contains internet, VoIP, network security, and technical support. Which concept does this illustrate?

132.en: A service offering is a formal description of one or more services designed to address the needs of a target consumer group, and it can include goods, access to resources, and service actions.

133.en: What is the purpose of the ITIL AI Capability Model?

134.en: To describe how service providers, service consumers, and other parties interact with AI to co-create value

135.en: To describe how organizations can assess and develop capabilities for effective use of AI

136.en: To prescribe specific AI technologies required for service development and management

137.en: To measure the performance of AI-enabled services against predefined service levels

138.en: The ITIL AI Capability Model helps outline AI's functional capabilities (like the 6C model) and connects them with assessing existing capabilities to address any gaps with clear action plans.

139.en: Which value chain activity is addressed by evaluating the quality of the resources and services sourced from a third party?

140.en: The "acquire" activity has specific success metrics, one of which is the quality of resources and services obtained.
